Timeline::isvalid¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline::isvalid() -> Series

Returns a boolean mask that marks the timestamps that are actually defined.

isvalid() is the positive-form validity check. Use it when the next operation should receive represented instants rather than NaT positions. That usually reads better than writing the same intent as !t.isnat().

The returned Series follows the exact shape of the source Timeline:

  • scalar timeline in, scalar boolean out

  • 1D timeline in, 1D boolean mask out

  • higher-rank timeline in, same higher-rank boolean structure out

Parameters¶

This method takes no parameters.

The main behavioral choice is conceptual:

  • use isvalid() when the positive case is the one you care about

  • use isnat() when the absent case is the one you care about

Returns¶

Series A boolean mask whose true positions correspond to defined timestamps and whose false positions correspond to NaT.

Notes¶

  • isvalid() is the complement of isnat().

  • It is especially useful ahead of where(...), filtering, or replacement logic where the “good rows” path is the default branch.

  • The method does not alter timezone information or timestamp values; it only inspects presence versus missingness.

Examples¶

Example 1. Build a validity mask from a Timeline containing absent instants.

auto keep = with_nat.isvalid();
std::cout << pluss::series::print(keep) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, true, false]

Example 2. Run the same check on a timeline where every timestamp is already defined.

auto keep = base.isvalid();
std::cout << pluss::series::print(keep) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, true, true, true]

Example 3. Use isvalid() when you want the positive branch to be explicit.

auto repaired = with_nat.where(with_nat.isvalid(), with_nat.floor("D"));
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(repaired) << "\n";

Output¶

This call keeps the original timestamp where the mask is true and falls back to the alternate timeline where the mask is false. See the verified where(...) behavior on the canonical page:

Timeline(shape=[4], tz=UTC)
[ 2024-11-01 00:00:00, NaT, 2024-12-31 00:00:00, NaT ]
